## Excursions to Pailón del Diablo waterfall from Baños

[Pailón del Diablo waterfall](/ecuador/place/pailon-del-diablo-waterfall/), known as the Devil's Cauldron, lies near Río Verde not far from [Baños](/ecuador/place/banos/). Water plunges into a narrow rocky gorge, producing powerful spray and clouds of mist. Visitors follow walking trails, stairs and viewpoints that lead closer to the cascade.

On our excursions, Pailón del Diablo forms part of the Waterfalls Route along the Pastaza River valley. Several itineraries are available, so pay attention to the final destination, the duration of the day and optional activities. Visiting the same waterfall does not make these programmes interchangeable.

## What makes the Devil's Cauldron special, and how do you visit?

Lush vegetation, dark rocks and the roar of water make this one of the most striking places on the eastern slopes of the Andes. To approach the waterfall, visitors descend along developed sections of trail. Viewpoints reveal the direction of the flow and the depth of the narrow gorge; spray can soak clothes and cameras.

The local Río Verde administration warns that access to popular waterfalls in the area involves steep paths and stairs, which may not suit everyone with reduced mobility. Surfaces can be slippery in rainy weather. Choose shoes with good grip and check the condition of the entrance and trail you plan to use.

## Which Ada Tours excursions include the waterfall?

[“Baños: Waterfalls Route and Swing at the End of the World”](/ecuador/banos/banos-waterfalls-and-swing/) visits Agoyán and [Manto de la Novia](/ecuador/place/manto-de-la-novia-waterfall/) waterfalls, Pailón del Diablo, [Pastaza Canyon](/ecuador/place/pastaza-canyon/) and [Casa del Árbol](/ecuador/place/casa-del-arbol/). With the onward transfer to Riobamba, the journey takes 8–9 hours and includes Russian-speaking assistance.

[“Baños: Waterfalls and Swing, Returning to Quito”](/ecuador/banos/banos-waterfalls-and-return-to-quito/) visits similar attractions but finishes in Quito. Including the transfers, it takes **11–12 hours**. This option suits travellers who need to return to the capital the same day rather than spend the night en route to Riobamba.

There is also a [two-day excursion from Quito to Baños](/ecuador/banos/banos-tour-from-quito-2-days/). It combines the waterfalls with other regional sites and an overnight stay, but accommodation arrangements and prices must be examined separately: a hotel is not listed among the included services.

| Option | How the journey ends |
|---|---|
| Waterfalls Route, 8–9 hours | Transfer to Riobamba |
| Waterfalls, 11–12 hours | Return to Quito |
| Two-day excursion | Programme with an overnight stay |

## What to see near Pailón del Diablo

The best-known combination in this area is [Agoyán](/ecuador/place/agoyan-waterfall/), [Manto de la Novia](/ecuador/place/manto-de-la-novia-waterfall/) and Pailón del Diablo. The stops offer different experiences: broad valley panoramas at some falls, a walk to viewpoints or a cable crossing at others.

[Pastaza Canyon](/ecuador/place/pastaza-canyon/) accompanies much of the route. Some excursions offer optional canopy rides above the canyon, paid separately at **$15 per person**. This is an extra service and must not be assumed to be included.

For views of the mountain valley, the [Swing at the End of the World](/ecuador/place/casa-del-arbol/) is another possible stop. As with the walking sections by the waterfalls, plan the visit according to the weather and participants' physical abilities.

## When is it most convenient to visit?

The Baños area has a humid climate, so heavy rain can affect visibility, trail conditions and comfort. No season guarantees dry steps or safe access to every viewpoint. Before departure, check that entrances are operating, any current restrictions and whether the planned route is accessible.

A waterproof jacket is useful for the walk, and electronics should be protected from spray. If there are young children or visitors with limited mobility in the group, discuss the difficulty of the descent beforehand: a guided excursion does not remove the physical terrain.

## Frequently asked questions about Pailón del Diablo

### Can the waterfall be visited on a day excursion?

Yes. It appears in several current programmes, including the [transfer to Riobamba](/ecuador/banos/banos-waterfalls-and-swing/) and [return to Quito](/ecuador/banos/banos-waterfalls-and-return-to-quito/) options.

### Is canopy riding above the canyon included?

In these excursions, canopy is listed as an optional activity at **$15 per person**, not a compulsory part of the programme.

### Is there a lot of walking at the waterfall?

Access to the viewpoints involves stairs and paths, some of which may be wet. The local administration specifically notes accessibility limitations on these sections.

### Which excursion returns to Quito in the evening?

[“Baños: Waterfalls and Swing, Returning to Quito”](/ecuador/banos/banos-waterfalls-and-return-to-quito/). The trip takes 11–12 hours.

## Papallacta excursion from Quito: thermal pools in the mountains

[Papallacta](/ecuador/place/papallacta/) is a mountainous area east of Ecuador's capital where hot springs lie among cloud-covered slopes. You can spend several hours in the water while watching clouds drift across green Andean ridges. The combination of highland travel and relaxation in the pools sets this excursion apart from a sightseeing tour of [Quito](/ecuador/place/quito-and-cotopaxi-volcano/).

We offer [“Papallacta: Andean Hot Springs from Quito”](/ecuador/quito-and-cotopaxi-volcano/papallacta-hot-springs-from-quito/). This is an **eight-hour excursion** with a Russian-speaking guide and transfers. Our itinerary mentions the Termas de Papallacta complex and its mineral-water pools.

## What is the thermal complex like?

Geothermally heated water is used in outdoor pools with different temperatures. The Ada Tours excursion description specifies **nine hot and three cold pools**, with water temperatures in the pools of approximately **36–40°C**. The number of pools available and operating arrangements in individual areas should be checked against the resort's latest information.

Papallacta is located at approximately 3,300 metres above sea level. The road from Quito crosses Andean highlands, where weather changes more quickly than in the lowlands. The complex may have several areas: general thermal pools, spa treatments, a restaurant and accommodation. Having these facilities does not mean every service is included in your chosen excursion.

## Which services and prices are specified by Ada Tours?

Our excursion includes **a Russian-speaking guide and transfers**. Lunch, medical or travel insurance and tips are paid for separately. Check the specific package and excursion page to establish whether pool admission and spa treatments are included; they should not be assumed from the words “hot springs” alone.

The listed basic excursion price is **$503**, with additional rates according to group size:

| Group size | Listed price |
|---|---|
| 2 people | $263 per person |
| 3 people | $233 per person |
| 4 people | $188 per person |

The basis for the basic amount is not specified, so it must not automatically be treated as a per-person rate. All amounts and their respective terms are shown on the [Papallacta excursion page](/ecuador/quito-and-cotopaxi-volcano/papallacta-hot-springs-from-quito/).

## How a Papallacta visit differs from sightseeing in Quito

In Quito, travellers usually choose the historic centre, museums and city walks; Papallacta is about mountain landscapes and thermal water. The road itself takes up a substantial part of the excursion day, so discuss the timetable and pool time if maximising relaxation is your priority.

If your journey includes several natural regions, a thermal day may provide a welcome change after active excursions. However, hot pools at altitude are not suitable for everyone. Anyone with cardiovascular conditions, pregnancy or other medical restrictions should ask a doctor beforehand whether extended immersion in hot water at high altitude is appropriate.

## What to bring and how to prepare

Bring swimwear, footwear suitable for wet surfaces, dry clothing and a warm jacket for leaving the pools. Even in cool air, sunlight can be intense at altitude. Do not assume that additional treatments or meals are already paid for.

Before your visit, check the complex's current hours, the availability of your chosen area and admission arrangements. The official Termas de Papallacta website publishes separate schedules for pools and spa facilities, which may differ.

## Frequently asked questions about Papallacta

### How long does the journey from Quito take?

Our excursion lasts **eight hours**, including transfers and the visit to Papallacta.

### Is a Russian-speaking guide provided?

Yes. Guide services and transfers are specified as included.

### Is lunch included in the price?

No. Lunch appears in the list of services excluded from the advertised package.

### What does the excursion cost for a group of four?

The price is **$188 per person** for a group of four. Rates for other group sizes are listed on the [excursion's own page](/ecuador/quito-and-cotopaxi-volcano/papallacta-hot-springs-from-quito/).

### Is a massage or private spa treatment included?

Massage and individual spa treatments are absent from the confirmed list of inclusions. Check the resort package and arrange any desired treatments in advance.

## Pastaza Canyon excursions: the Waterfalls Route from Baños

[Pastaza Canyon](/ecuador/place/pastaza-canyon/) lies in eastern Ecuador. Here the river cuts through green mountain slopes, with one waterfall after another appearing along the road from [Baños](/ecuador/place/banos/) towards Puyo. The route is known as the Waterfalls Route: travellers stop at viewpoints, descend towards cascades and, in some places, cross the gorge by cable car.

We include the canyon in several standalone excursions around Baños. The main choice concerns onward logistics: after visiting the waterfalls, you can continue towards Riobamba or return to Quito. The two options differ in duration and final destination.

## Which waterfalls are visited along the way?

Our routes include [Agoyán Waterfall](/ecuador/place/agoyan-waterfall/), [Manto de la Novia](/ecuador/place/manto-de-la-novia-waterfall/) and [Pailón del Diablo](/ecuador/place/pailon-del-diablo-waterfall/), also known as the Devil's Cauldron. Each site shows a different side of the gorge: a broad flow of water, a crossing of the valley, or a close approach to a powerful cascade via steps.

A cable crossing is possible in the Manto de la Novia area. It is explicitly mentioned in the excursion descriptions; confirm the specific conditions of using it on the chosen date. Near the Devil's Cauldron, the walk involves wet steps and developed trails. Seeing the canyon does not require entering the river independently; the main views can be enjoyed from permitted viewpoints.

## Which excursions travel through Pastaza?

[“Baños: Waterfalls Route and Swing at the End of the World”](/ecuador/banos/banos-waterfalls-and-swing/) takes **8–9 hours with the onward transfer to Riobamba**. In addition to waterfalls and the gorge, the route includes [Casa del Árbol](/ecuador/place/casa-del-arbol/) and its swing, time in Baños and Russian-speaking assistance.

[“Baños: Waterfalls and Swing, Returning to Quito”](/ecuador/banos/banos-waterfalls-and-return-to-quito/) covers a similar series of waterfalls and viewpoints but ends back in the capital. Including transfers, the total duration is **11–12 hours**. Approximately 3.5 hours are allocated for the Baños–Quito transfer.

| Excursion option | End of the day |
|---|---|
| 8–9 hours | Transfer to Riobamba |
| 11–12 hours | Return to Quito |

Both are suitable if you want to see the valley's waterfalls, but the logistics after the canyon are different. They should not be substituted for one another if the next night's accommodation has already been planned in a particular city.

## Canopy rides over the canyon: what is included?

On both excursions, an optional canopy ride above Pastaza Canyon can be booked for **$15 per person**. It is an extra activity, not included among the basic services. Participation depends on the operator's rules, weather and personal readiness.

The wider area offers other active pursuits, but references to rafting, canyoning or bungee jumping in general descriptions of Baños do not make those activities part of these excursions. To avoid confusion, compare the included and excluded services on the specific product page.

## Preparing for the road and viewpoints

The canyon is humid and weather may change during the outing. Stones and stairs near waterfalls are often wet, so shoes with good grip are useful. On narrow walking sections, follow permitted paths and keep a safe distance from the edge. For children or people with reduced mobility, confirm access to each site in advance.

If a cable crossing or optional canopy ride is planned, separately check opening times, the equipment's condition and the operator's current restrictions. Do not assume that these attractions can be used independently without supervision.

## Frequently asked questions about Pastaza excursions

### Which waterfalls are explicitly listed in Ada Tours programmes?

[Agoyán](/ecuador/place/agoyan-waterfall/), [Manto de la Novia](/ecuador/place/manto-de-la-novia-waterfall/) and [the Devil's Cauldron](/ecuador/place/pailon-del-diablo-waterfall/). These stops feature in the two principal published options.

### Can I return to Quito on the same day?

Yes. There is an [excursion returning to Quito](/ecuador/banos/banos-waterfalls-and-return-to-quito/) that lasts 11–12 hours including transfers.

### Is canopy riding included in the price?

No. In our programmes, canopy is paid for separately at **$15 per person**.

### How does Pastaza Canyon differ from a single stop at Pailón?

The canyon covers a lengthy natural route along the river and several waterfalls. [Pailón del Diablo](/ecuador/place/pailon-del-diablo-waterfall/) is one cascade with walking paths and viewpoints within this larger excursion area.

## Agoyán Waterfall: the first part of the Waterfalls Route near Baños

[Agoyán](/ecuador/place/agoyan-waterfall/) lies in the Pastaza River valley near [Baños](/ecuador/place/banos/). Water descends into a mountain gorge between rocky walls, surrounded by lush vegetation. The waterfall is part of the popular Waterfalls Route east of Baños.

This excursion reveals the landscape's gradual change from the Andean highlands to wetter valleys. Agoyán makes a natural early stop on the route, rather than a standalone destination for a multi-day journey.

## Why the waterfall looks different from day to day

The Agoyán hydroelectric power station operates on the Pastaza River upstream of the waterfall. The state energy company CELEC confirms that it uses water from this river and is located in the Baños area. The visible flow therefore depends not only on rainfall but also on how water is regulated.

Postcards and older photographs may show a more powerful cascade than visitors see on a particular day. Promising identical width and flow year-round would be misleading. Even when less water is flowing, the Pastaza valley remains striking, with a deep gorge, mountain slopes and humid vegetation.

Guidebooks give varying figures for the waterfall's height, so it is more useful to consider accessible viewpoints and the conditions you will actually see than to rely on a disputed number of metres.

## How to view Agoyán on an excursion

The route generally follows the road from Baños along the Pastaza Valley. Depending on the operator and season, stops at viewpoints, short walks or additional activities may be offered.

Distinguish **viewing the waterfall** from independently paid activities. Cable crossings, zip lines and other ways to approach the gorge are not included in every programme and can depend on weather and operating conditions. Check specific arrangements, age restrictions and physical requirements before purchasing an excursion.

For a typical stop, bring closed shoes, a waterproof outer layer and protection for your camera. Spray, wet paths and wind at open viewpoints call for care. Do not cross barriers for a photograph.

## Which waterfalls can you visit after Agoyán?

The Waterfalls Route continues farther down the valley. One well-known site is [Manto de la Novia Waterfall](/ecuador/place/manto-de-la-novia-waterfall/), whose cascade among green slopes offers a different scene. Another stop is [the Devil's Cauldron](/ecuador/place/pailon-del-diablo-waterfall/), with a different approach and views of turbulent water.

Agoyán, Manto de la Novia and the Devil's Cauldron are especially rewarding as a combination if the itinerary allows time at each. With limited time, two stops with proper walks may be better than trying to see every waterfall through a vehicle window.

Outings often start in [Baños](/ecuador/place/banos/), which offers other nature and adventure activities. Compare our programmes through the [Ecuador tours catalogue](/ecuador/tour/), but check the exact waterfalls and paid activities on each route.

## When to visit and what to plan for

The Pastaza Valley can be humid even when it is sunny above Baños. Rain changes the state of paths and visibility from viewpoints. Exposed cable crossings and attractions may be restricted due to the weather, regardless of tourist season.

Allow some flexibility for transfers and walks. If Agoyán is part of a full day featuring several cascades, find out in advance how much time is allocated to viewing it and which stops are planned directly by the road.

## Frequently asked questions about Agoyán Waterfall

### Where is Agoyán Waterfall?

In the Pastaza River valley near [Baños](/ecuador/place/banos/) in Ecuador, along the route east of the town.

### Why does Agoyán sometimes look less powerful?

Upstream, a hydroelectric plant uses water from the Pastaza River. The visible flow depends in part on water management.

### Can Agoyán be combined with other waterfalls?

Yes. [Manto de la Novia](/ecuador/place/manto-de-la-novia-waterfall/) and [the Devil's Cauldron](/ecuador/place/pailon-del-diablo-waterfall/) lie along the same road. Time for viewing depends on the chosen excursion.

### Is zip-lining included with a visit to the waterfall?

Not necessarily. Cable crossings and other activities may cost extra and have restrictions; check the specific programme.

## Tours via Agoyán Waterfall: choosing an Ecuador itinerary

[Agoyán Waterfall](/ecuador/place/agoyan-waterfall/) lies east of Baños in the Pastaza River valley. The area is known as the Waterfalls Route: the road descends from the Andes towards the more humid slopes leading to the Amazon. Along the way are rocky gorges, viewpoints and several different waterfalls.

Our catalogue contains {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}} with Agoyán among the route's main destinations. But **appearing on the overall route does not guarantee a long, separate visit to the waterfall's base**: some journeys are organised as a sightseeing drive along the Baños–Puyo road or stops at several natural sites.

## What to know about the waterfall itself

Agoyán lies approximately 7 km from Baños on the road towards Puyo. Its waters are connected with the Pastaza River. A nearby hydroelectric complex affects the distribution of water flow. The waterfall can therefore look different: when floodgates are opened there is noticeably more water, while at other times the flow is more modest.

This is a practical difference from expecting a **constantly powerful cascade**. Viewpoints reveal the landscape, but the precise volume of water depends on natural conditions and reservoir operations.

Another well-known stop near Baños is [the Devil's Cauldron waterfall](/ecuador/place/pailon-del-diablo-waterfall/). It has its own visitor route, and its location and walking experience differ from Agoyán. An itinerary combining waterfalls may include both, but you should check the actual stop at each one.

## Which itineraries include Agoyán?

**Active hiking programme.** [“Active Ecuador and Trekking”](/ecuador/tour/active-ecuador-trekking/) combines Andean hikes, Quilotoa crater lake, Chimborazo and the more humid Baños area. After the mountain stages, the itinerary passes through Papallacta and Puyo to the Waterfalls Route. Agoyán is one natural stop on this journey; the sporting activities are determined by the specific days, not merely by the waterfall's inclusion.

**New Year itinerary.** [“Complete Ecuador for New Year”](/ecuador/tour/complete-ecuador-new-year/) lasts 11 days, from 30 December 2026 to 9 January 2027, covering the Andes and Galápagos Islands. The day scheduled for 2 January 2027 is “Baños, Waterfalls and Riobamba”, explicitly listing Agoyán, Manto de la Novia and the Devil's Cauldron. This is an example of a clearly specified sequence of nature stops.

**Ecuador and the Galápagos.** The [17-day adventure tour](/ecuador/tour/ecuador-galapagos-adventure-17-days/) combines Andean natural regions, the Waterfalls Route and the islands. It allows more time to travel through Ecuador, but the waterfall should not be considered a standalone sporting excursion. Other options include [“Best of Ecuador: Guaranteed Departures”](/ecuador/tour/best-of-ecuador-guaranteed-departures/) and a [tour of Ecuador and the Galápagos' protected landscapes](/ecuador/tour/ecuador-galapagos-nature-discovery/).

Those interested in varied natural environments can compare [“Ecuador, Galápagos and Humpback Whales”](/ecuador/tour/ecuador-galapagos-humpback-whales/) and [“Ecuador: Andes, Amazon and Galápagos”](/ecuador/tour/ecuador-galapagos-islands/). On those journeys, the Baños area is only one part of a wider route; the details of animal-watching activities and flights to the islands must be assessed separately.

## Choosing by interests and duration

If **active time in the Andes** is your main goal, choose a route with confirmed hikes and genuine physical demands. Agoyán then becomes a nature stop after the mountain stage.

If you want to **visit several waterfalls in one day**, examine the Baños excursion section: the sequence, number of stops, transport and walks. The New Year itinerary explicitly names several waterfalls; the exact selection may vary on others.

If you also plan to visit **the Galápagos Islands**, time on the mainland is reduced by the flights and island portion. Find out how days are divided between Baños, Cuenca and the Galápagos rather than choosing solely by the length of a tour's name.

## Visiting conditions and safety

The road runs through a humid river valley. Waterfall stops call for shoes with good grip and rain protection. Possible suspension crossings, tarabita cable cars, canopy rides or cycling around Baños **should not be considered included Ada Tours services** unless specifically listed in the selected itinerary. These are separate activities with their own rules.

We help select a route by duration, number of nature stops and combination with the Andes, Amazon or islands. For photographs and waterfall viewing, account for variations in water flow and weather beforehand.

## Frequently asked questions about tours through Agoyán

### Does every itinerary guarantee a separate excursion to Agoyán Waterfall?

Not necessarily. The catalogue reflects the main geography of a trip, while the actual stops and time at each are set by the itinerary.

### Why can Agoyán look different on different days?

The Pastaza River supplies a hydroelectric complex, so the volume of water depends on the facility's operations as well as natural conditions.

### Can Agoyán be combined with other Baños waterfalls?

Yes. Several programmes include the Waterfalls Route. The New Year itinerary explicitly lists Agoyán, Manto de la Novia and the Devil's Cauldron together.

### Is a 17-day tour worthwhile for just one waterfall?

A longer journey makes sense if you also want the Andes and Galápagos Islands. For a single nature stop, such an extensive route is excessive.
